subject: Transportation Systems
title: Just-in-Time Delivery
description: A short lesson to help you apply Just-in-Time Delivery.

hook.text: Toyota figured out that storing parts costs money. What if parts arrived exactly when needed—not before?

buildup.text: Just-in-time manufacturing eliminates warehouse stockpiles. Parts arrive hours before assembly.

discovery.text: JIT slashes storage costs and reduces waste. Factories operate with minimal inventory.

twist.text: Covid exposed JIT's weakness. When one supplier shut down, entire production lines went dark for months.

climax.text: Companies are now adding buffer stock—'just in case.' Efficiency and resilience are competing priorities.

punchline.text: Just in time works perfectly—until it doesn't.

quiz.question: What is the main risk of just-in-time supply chains?
options: Any disruption at one supplier can halt entire production lines
